root_cause.summary: The canonical migration snapshot ended the PL/pgSQL dollar-quoted function body without the required SQL statement semicolon before subsequent REVOKE/GRANT statements.
causes: live function definition text was copied into a migration and concatenated with privilege statements without restoring the statement terminator
runtime deployment had already succeeded independently, so the repository migration syntax defect was not visible until clean replay

prevention_rules: Every CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION ... AS $function$ block in a migration must end with $function$; before any following statement.
Security-definer migration snapshots must be clean-replay parsable and carry explicit revoke/grant boundaries.
Runtime success never substitutes for clean repository migration replay.
Material recovery must include Brain learning, activity ledger and human documentation in the same lineage.

evidence.failure: syntax error at or near revoke because function statement terminator was missing

outcome.intended_state: Canonical migration replays from a clean environment, preserves terminal provider-side-effect behavior, and remains service-role-only.
